questions.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x={c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 10-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}10 & -3 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x={c}_{1}+4{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 16\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 3 & 16\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 3 & 16\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 16-3\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}16 & -5 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -5 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -5 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\},\,C=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given above. Find $[x]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ relative to the basis $C.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 5-5\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
